title: Probability
seo_title: Probability – SSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the probability of single events; use the sample space; find probabilities of combined events using addition and multiplication. (summary of the NERDC SSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 maths worksheets on probability: single events, dice, cards and bags, sample spaces, and combined events. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Probability = number of favourable outcomes ÷ number of possible outcomes.
  • Probabilities are from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
  • For two events one after the other, multiply; for “either … or” (mutually exclusive), add.

Examples

Example

A bag has 3 red and 5 blue balls

Red: 3 out of 8

Answer: P(red) = 3/8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when you should multiply“And then” means multiply.
Forgetting that the ball is not replacedTake 1 from the total for the second pick.
Probability bigger than 1Check: it can never be more than 1.

items.q: Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are added. What is the probability of an even sum?
items.e: Draw a 6 × 6 sample space: 36 equally likely outcomes. 18 of them give an even sum, so P = 1836 = 12.

items.q: Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are multiplied. What is the probability of an even product?
items.e: Draw a 6 × 6 sample space: 36 equally likely outcomes. 27 of them give an even product, so P = 2736 = 34.

items.q: Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are subtracted (larger − smaller). What is the probability of an even difference?
